subject: stan_lmer: uniform priors on the coefficients

messages.author: b6fd2925353976cd
messages.subject: stan_lmer: uniform priors on the coefficients
parts:
Hi all,

How can one define a uniform prior on the coefficients in a linear mixed model? I want to say something like:

mstan<-stan_glmer(target~condition+(1+condition|subject)+(condition|item.ID),
                  family=binomial(),
                  prior_intercept=uniform(-10,10),
                  prior=uniform(-10,10),
                  prior_covariance=decov(regularization=2),
                  exp1ab,
                  chains=4,
                  iter=2000,
                  cores=4)

thanks,

Shravan Vasishth

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: stan_lmer: uniform priors on the coefficients
parts:
Hi Shravan, 

If you set prior=NULL it will get rid of the prior entirely (and so the priors will be improper uniforms), but for reasons described by Ben (see here: https://github.com/stan-dev/rstanarm/issues/58) we haven't implemented a way for users to use a bounded uniform prior.

Jonah

Hi Shravan,

That seems reasonable and the more I think about it the more I'm open to the idea of including functionality like this that is intended solely for pedagogical use if it's accompanied by warnings. So far we've been thinking of rstanarm as a way to promote best practices, providing as few ways as possible to go astray, so to speak, but I do see the educational value of allowing some things to be done the "wrong way".

I'm curious what the other developers think about this, and feedback on this issue from you and other current and potential rstanarm users is very much appreciated.

Jonah

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: stan_lmer: uniform priors on the coefficients
parts:
On Thursday, January 28, 2016 at 10:52:46 AM UTC-5, Jonah Gabry wrote:
I'm curious what the other developers think about this, and feedback on this issue from you and other current and potential rstanarm users is very much appreciated.

I'm reluctant to put knowingly wrong things into rstanarm because most users will not have an instructional environment where they can learn why it is wrong. The perils of bounded uniform priors can sort of be demonstrated by doing prior = NULL, as.matrix(), and then deleting draws where the coefficients on the common parameters fall outside given bounds. But it can also be demonstrated in a simple Stan program that estimates a linear model that just has one predictor and no group-specific parameters. Finally, you can get the rethinking package to generate a Stan program that has uniform priors. I'm not sure about brms.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan_lmer: uniform priors on the coefficients
parts:
I agree — there’s no point in teaching bad priors in rstanarm if rstanarm doesn’t
allow them!  The utility of teaching about these pathologies arises when users
are building their own models, which means not using rstanarm but rather Rstan
proper.  If it’s this hard to do, you probably shouldn’t be doing it — I’m sure there’s
some corollary to the Folk Theorem that covers it.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: no uniform priors
parts:
On Thursday, January 28, 2016 at 5:33:35 PM UTC-5, Andrew Gelman wrote:
Uniform is a default.  If you have a bounded parameter and you don’t specify a prior, uniform is what is being done. There is never a reason to use a uniform on a space different from the bounds of the parameter.

To clarify --- because Shravan was originally asking about rstanarm --- there is no option in rstanarm to put additional bounds on the parameters in its pre-compiled Stan programs. Either the parameters are unbounded on both sides in the case of coefficients, bounded only from below at zero in the case of standard deviations, etc. Consequently, we have not implemented and do not plan to implement proper uniform priors, although in most cases it is possible to utilize an improper uniform prior by specifying prior = NULL in the R function that calls it.

Ben

Uniform is a default.  If you have a bounded parameter and you don’t specify a prior, uniform is what is being done. There is never a reason to use a uniform on a space different from the bounds of the parameter.

To clarify --- because Shravan was originally asking about rstanarm --- there is no option in rstanarm to put additional bounds on the parameters in its pre-compiled Stan programs. Either the parameters are unbounded on both sides in the case of coefficients, bounded only from below at zero in the case of standard deviations, etc. Consequently, we have not implemented and do not plan to implement proper uniform priors, although in most cases it is possible to utilize an improper uniform prior by specifying prior = NULL in the R function that calls it.
